Assert that every row meets a condition

Source: R/ensure_all.R
ensure_all.Rd

The positive form of ensure_none(): state what must hold instead of what must not occur. data itself is returned, so the pipeline continues with all rows:

Usage

ensure_all(data, ..., success_msg = NULL, warn_msg = NULL, abort_msg = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

...

Conditions every row must meet, written as in dplyr::filter().

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when rows fail the condition and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the condition.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

df |>
  ensure_all(amount >= 0, abort_msg = "Amounts must not be negative") |>
  ensure_all(year %in% 2015:2024) |>
  mutate(...)

Why both ensure_all() and ensure_none()

The two are not each other's negation, because they treat a missing value differently. A row violates ensure_all() unless the condition is TRUE, so a row where it is NA is a violation: the rule cannot be shown to hold. In ensure_none() such a row passes, as it would in dplyr::filter().

df <- data.frame(amount = c(10, -5, NA))

ensure_none(df, amount < 0)   # 1 row: -5
ensure_all(df, amount >= 0)   # 2 rows: -5 and NA

Use ensure_all() when a value has to be present and right, and ensure_none() when a missing value is acceptable or is a separate rule with its own message.

Several conditions must all hold, so a row is a violation when any of them is FALSE or NA.

See also

ensure_none(), ensure_empty(), tally_violations(), checkpoints

Examples

mtcars |>
  ensure_all(cyl %in% c(4, 6, 8)) |>
  ensure_all(mpg > 15, warn_msg = "Thirsty cars") |>
  nrow()
#> ✔ All rows meet cyl %in% c(4, 6, 8)
#> Warning: Thirsty cars
#> ℹ 6 rows found:
#>       mpg   cyl  disp    hp  drat    wt  qsec    vs    am  gear  carb
#>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>   1  14.3     8   360   245  3.21  3.57  15.8     0     0     3     4
#>   2  10.4     8   472   205  2.93  5.25  18.0     0     0     3     4
#>   3  10.4     8   460   215  3     5.42  17.8     0     0     3     4
#>   4  14.7     8   440   230  3.23  5.34  17.4     0     0     3     4
#>   5  13.3     8   350   245  3.73  3.84  15.4     0     0     3     4
#>   # ℹ 1 more row
#> ℹ Wrap the check in violations() to get all rows.
#> [1] 32

# A missing value is a violation here, but not in ensure_none()
df <- data.frame(amount = c(10, -5, NA))
ensure_all(df, amount >= 0)
#> Warning: Found rows that do not meet amount >= 0
#> ℹ 2 rows found:
#>     amount
#>      <dbl>
#>   1     -5
#>   2     NA
ensure_none(df, amount < 0)
#> Warning: Found rows where amount < 0
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>     amount
#>      <dbl>
#>   1     -5
